entries.name: Build Waveform
entries.description: Builds an analog waveform or modifies an existing waveform. If you do not wire the waveform input, the function creates a new waveform based on the components you wire. If you wire the waveform input, the function modifies the waveform based on the components you wire. Functions © National Instruments 797

terminals.name: waveform
terminals.description: waveform is the analog waveform you want to edit. If you do not wire an existing waveform, the function creates a new waveform based on the components you wire.

terminals.name: t0
terminals.description: t0 specifies the start time of the waveform.

terminals.name: dt
terminals.description: dt specifies the time interval in seconds between data points in the waveform.

terminals.name: Y
terminals.description: Y specifies the data values of the waveform.

terminals.name: attributes
terminals.description: attributes sets the names and values of all waveform attributes. The value of this parameter is not used. Instead, the variant attributes are used to define the waveform attributes. You also can use the Set Waveform Attribute function to set the name and value of a single attribute.

terminals.name: output waveform
terminals.description: waveform is the resulting waveform. If you did not wire an existing waveform, this is a new waveform. If you wired an existing waveform, this is the edited waveform.

entries.name: Get Waveform Components
entries.description: Returns the analog waveform you specify. You specify components by clicking on the center of the output terminal and selecting the component you want.

terminals.name: waveform
terminals.description: waveform is the waveform from which you want to retrieve components.

terminals.name: t0
terminals.description: t0 returns the trigger time of the waveform.

terminals.name: dt
terminals.description: dt returns the time interval in seconds between data points in the waveform.

terminals.name: Y
terminals.description: Y returns the data values of the waveform.

terminals.name: attributes
terminals.description: attributes returns the names and values of all waveform attributes. You also can use the Get Waveform Attribute VI to retrieve the names and values of all attributes or the value of a single attribute.

entries.name: Set Waveform Attribute Function
entries.description: Adds or replaces a waveform attribute. You can use any type of data for the value of the attribute. Functions 798 ni.com

terminals.name: waveform
terminals.description: waveform is the waveform for which you want to add or replace an attribute.

terminals.name: name
terminals.description: name is the name of the attribute.

terminals.name: value
terminals.description: value is the value of the attribute. This input is polymorphic, so you can wire any data to it.

terminals.name: error in (no error)
terminals.description: error in describes error conditions that occur before this node runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.

terminals.name: waveform out
terminals.description: waveform out is the waveform with the new or replaced attribute.

terminals.name: replaced
terminals.description: replaced indicates if an attribute was overwritten.

terminals.name: error out
terminals.description: error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.

entries.name: Get Waveform Attribute Function
entries.description: Retrieves the names and values of all attributes or the value of a single attribute, depending on whether you wire the name parameter. Attributes can be channel names. The connector pane displays the default data types for this polymorphic function.

terminals.name: waveform
terminals.description: waveform is the waveform for which you want to retrieve an attribute(s) and value(s).

terminals.name: name
terminals.description: name is the name of the attribute whose value you want to retrieve. Do not wire this parameter if you want to retrieve all the attributes associated with the specified waveform. If you wire name , the names output changes to a Boolean output found , the array output values changes to an output called value of the same type as default value , and the function searches for only the specified attribute.

terminals.name: default value (empty Variant)
terminals.description: default value is a value and data type that you specify. If the function does not find the attribute specified in name , it returns the default value . If you wire default value , you must wire name .

terminals.name: error in (no error)
terminals.description: error in describes error conditions that occur before this node runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.

terminals.name: duplicate waveform
terminals.description: duplicate waveform is the waveform data you input in waveform .

terminals.name: names
terminals.description: names returns a 1D array containing the names of all attributes associated with the waveform. If you wire the name parameter, this output changes to a Boolean value found . found returns TRUE if the function finds the attribute that you specify in name .

terminals.name: values
terminals.description: values returns a 1D array containing the values associated with each attribute of the specified waveform in variant format. You must unflatten each attribute value to an appropriate data type. If you wire name , this output changes to a single variant value . If the function does not find the attribute that you specify in name , it returns the value passed to default value .

terminals.name: error out
terminals.description: error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
